result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, whatever the rest of the name is. I haven't tested the new cases directly. I ran `mvn -o -pl codeanalyzer test -Dtest='*Scoping*'`, which passed with no output, but I didn't check how many tests matched that filter.

The change is in `addTestConventions` in `ScopingConventions.java`. The two mock patterns used to allow only ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-` and space, and they required at least one character after `mock`. I replaced that character class with `[^/]*`:

- `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`
- `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`

That covers plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/`. The match stays inside one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` are still not test code. `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all still match.

I didn't change anything for backslash paths. As far as I could tell from `SourceFileFilter.java`, paths are converted from `\` to `/` before they are matched, so Windows-style paths go through the same patterns.

Nothing is committed.
